hollow_delve_depth.generation_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Input image 1 is the edit target.
Restyle the supplied game layer to the materials, palette and formations below. Preserve its canvas aspect ratio, orthographic camera, independent layer role, horizontal continuation and overall occupied/empty layout. Replace conflicting surface details and shapes; this is not merely a color tint.
Keep the image completely opaque.
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: independently scrolling depth layer for a claustrophobic side-scrolling game interior
Primary request: Low earthy limestone cave
Materials: An ordinary compact underground cave of warm brown limestone, weathered earthen rock, subdued tan sediment bands and dusty cracks. Broad irregular rounded rock masses and shallow ledges, with occasional old brown timber. Natural rock buttresses rather than brick columns or arches. Ceiling: a heavy low gently uneven brown rock shelf; mostly blunt rounded underside, no hanging needles or icicle teeth. No stalagmite forest, dense stalactites, crystals, blue mineral crusts or dramatic fantasy formations.
Composition: Opaque distant recess layer only. A close horizontal band of dark shallow recesses in an enclosed passage, interrupted by dim silhouettes of distant supports. Subtle atmospheric depth and a narrow value range. No enormous chamber, vertical abyss, soaring pillars or receding corridor. No foreground ceiling, floor, nearby wall piers, props or characters. Fill the entire image; any visible recess has an enclosed back.
Camera: strict orthographic side view along a horizontal tunnel, parallel to the image plane. The passage continues sideways off both edges.
Style/medium: Weathered dark fantasy pixel art. Broad readable shapes, deliberate stepped color clusters, restrained outlines and a small muted palette. Material identity comes from silhouette and a few grouped marks. Match the visible pixel size and grouped shading of the authored player and enemies. Broad connected color clusters, a few stepped material shades and restrained local contrast behind actors; distant layers use a narrower value range. Preserve layered depth and readable material edges at the shared world pixel density.
Color palette: Earth brown #554334, umber #382a21, warm charcoal #211b16, dusty warm gray #7d7060, muted tan #95816a and dark old timber #493727. No blue, cyan, teal or purple cast.
Lighting: Dim neutral-to-warm reflected light with soft brown shadows and restrained highlights. A typical earthy underground passage, neither icy nor orange-glowing.
Canvas: 640 by 360 logical units; generate a large image with width at least 1536 pixels and this aspect ratio.
Pixel scale: match the authored player and enemy sprites at 1.5 texture pixels per game unit; a 64-unit standing actor is approximately 96 visible pixels tall. Use deliberate connected color clusters and a few stepped shade bands, with no photographic grain or dithering. Keep scenery contrast below the actors and preserve the biome palette. The runtime texture is 960 by 540 pixels. A larger generation master is allowed; compose its details for this final pixel grid.
Opacity: completely opaque edge-to-edge image.
If a reference image is supplied, use it for pixel texture density and restrained shading only; keep the requested indoor subject and enclosed composition.
Avoid: photorealism, intricate microtexture, dense cracks or hatching, single-pixel speckle, dithering, dramatic spotlights, bloom, soft airbrushed edges, text, watermarks, UI, painted checkerboard, isometric or overhead view, a road receding to a vanishing point, tiny-resolution upscaling, flat featureless polygons, harsh white highlights, vast cave expanses, soaring ceilings, long vanishing-point corridors, characters
Actor art direction: Input image 2 is an authored character STYLE REFERENCE ONLY; Input image 3 is an authored character STYLE REFERENCE ONLY.
Redraw the scenery in the same deliberately drawn pixel-art language as these actors. Keep the planned scene, biome colors, silhouettes and transparency; do not insert characters or copy their equipment into the scenery.
Use clear stepped contours, broad connected color patches, and three or four discrete shades per material. Replace photographic mottling, grain, airbrushed volume and tiny highlights with sparse purposeful pixel clusters. The change must be visible at gameplay size, not only when zooming into a texture.
Do not merely resize, blur, recolor, posterize or apply a pixelation filter to the old artwork. Draw fresh simplified material faces and clean edges with restrained background contrast.
